Overall, I like this one. It's a cool concept with neat effects. That being said, your [DATA EXPUNGED] was a bit sloppy and your tone was a bit off in a few places (For example, the line "Only due to Agent [DATA EXPUNGED]’s quick thinking and uncommon valor was [DATA EXPUNGED] and the object brought into containment" should not be in an SCP report, in my opinion).

Still nice job overall, upvoted.

item.content:encoded:
All class-D personnel required for use of SCP-842 are to be escorted by no less than two Level 2 Security personnel.

I thought that security personnel were all Level 3?

Foundation casualties numbered over █ agents and █ class-D personnel.

At first I was wondering why in the world the Foundation would use class-D personnel to help them do a raid. Then I realized that the agents could herd the class-D's in front of them to set off traps and such. Brrrrr.

Testing on the quantum or stellar scale has been indefinitely suspended.

Maybe self referential testing should be banned as well? You know there has to be at least one researcher who'd wonder "What would happen if we used SCP-842-1 to view SCP-842-1?"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think the most horrifying thing about this is that the article treats this as an acceptable, viable surveillance system that should be used regularly. At least, that's how it comes off. Only thing detracting from the "academic" feel the writing should have is the explicit use of "she." I think it should be more gender-neutral, but that's just me. Over all though, I liked it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Suitably horrible trade-off, given how useful this thing would be otherwise. I do have to wonder about all the screaming, though… it's fine that 842 is keeping the subjects alive through a procedure that would otherwise kill them, but screaming involves use of the lungs, which would presumably be outside the subject's control (along with the rest of their organs) after they become 842-1.

That 842 would allow its subjects to vocalize despite needing their mouths as a "speaker" just seems out of place compared to the effectiveness of the rest of the "display", and kind of over the top from a horror perspective. I think it might be even more unnerving if the subject was clearly conscious and alarmed but unable to communicate, sort of like those "awake on the operating table" amnesia mishap stories you hear about from time to time. Not a huge issue, though- it's still getting my upvote.

item.title: (no title)

I can almost imagine a researcher using it to see what the traffic home is like, and be subsequently demoted to Keter duty as a result.
